title: Insert a reading entry
summary: An INSERT writes values at a primary-key address.
introduction: An INSERT writes values at a primary-key address. Your task: Insert a different day for the same reader.
learningObjectives: Insert a different day for the same reader.
Explain the example for insert a reading entry

blocks.text: An INSERT writes values at a primary-key address. Writing the same key again updates those supplied values rather than making a duplicate row.
Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.
Read the code step by step

items: The column list supplies both primary-key parts and the stored facts.
The same reader-and-day key identifies the same row on a later write.

blocks.text: Mia's entry for that day stores Moon Trip and 20 pages.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Know the full primary key. Reusing it can overwrite values at the same record address.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Insert a different day for the same reader.
